quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results (CFO Lynn Hutkin): total sales were $210.7 million, up 25% from the prior-year quarter, with broad-based growth led by defense and data solutions and a distribution-channel rebound (channel sales at the highest level since mid-2022, per CEO Farouq Tuweiq). Gross margin was 39.9%, up 120 basis points year over year on operating leverage, partly offset by higher material costs and unfavorable FX. Adjusted EBITDA was $48.9 million versus $35.2 million a year ago (up approximately 39%), a 23.2% margin versus 20.9%.
quarterly_data.figure: Q2 2026 sales $210.7 million (+25% YoY); gross margin 39.9% (+120 bps); adjusted EBITDA $48.9 million vs $35.2 million (approximately 39%); margin 23.2% vs 20.9%

quarterly_data.signal: Segment results (CFO Lynn Hutkin): Aerospace Defense and Rugged Solutions (ADRS) revenue was $111 million, up $18.6 million or 20.6%, led by defense at $66.5 million (up 28.4%), with industrial gains through distribution and a decline in commercial air; ADRS gross margin was 41.1% versus 41.4%. Industrial Technology & Data Solutions (ITDS) revenue was $100 million, up $23.8 million or 31.1%, with gross margin 38.8% versus 36.6% on favorable mix and utilization, partly offset by the weaker U.S. dollar against the renminbi raising costs at Chinese manufacturing sites; transportation declined modestly. Space revenue was $3 million, up slightly (CEO).
quarterly_data.figure: ADRS $111 million (+20.6%), defense $66.5 million (+28.4%), ADRS gross margin 41.1% vs 41.4%; ITDS $100 million (+31.1%), ITDS gross margin 38.8% vs 36.6%; space $3 million

quarterly_data.signal: Data solutions / high-performance computing ramp (CFO Lynn Hutkin, CEO Farouq Tuweiq): data solutions sales were about $58 million in Q2 2026, up from $38 million a year earlier - a $20.7 million or 55% increase - and 'higher demand within data solutions includes the beginning of a ramp related to recent project wins in the high-performance computing space'; the dataMate acquisition (March 2026) contributed $4.4 million. CEO: 'we are seeing programmatic wins that were achieved some time ago start to ramp', feeding revenue as customers deploy their products; bookings and planning discussions with partners indicate healthy upward trends, and 'we expect further ramp as we close out the year and into next year.'
quarterly_data.figure: data solutions about $58 million (vs $38 million; +$20.7 million or 55%); dataMate $4.4 million

quarterly_data.signal: Bookings (CEO Farouq Tuweiq, CFO Lynn Hutkin): bookings exceeded sales for the sixth consecutive quarter; the positive book-to-bill has been broad-based across both segments, most product lines and most end markets, concentrated in defense, data solutions and the distribution channel, where component products (fuses, integrated connector modules and RF connectors) led a rebound that was particularly strong in Q2.
quarterly_data.figure: book-to-bill above one for six consecutive quarters

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 outlook (CEO Farouq Tuweiq, CFO Lynn Hutkin): sales projected at $205 to $225 million with gross margin of 39% to 41%, driven by defense, data solutions and higher component demand through distribution. Price increases placed on new orders in February-March should start to benefit Q3 (not fully, since they ship over time) and Q4; FX pressure from the renminbi and Israeli shekel is not expected to worsen. SG&A is expected at approximately $34 million to $35 million in future quarters. The CEO flagged a coming 'revenue rotation', mainly in ITDS data solutions, emphasizing higher-growth, better-margin business over larger lower-margin products starting into Q4 and 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 2026 sales $205 to $225 million; gross margin 39% to 41%; SG&A approximately $34 million to $35 million per quarter

quarterly_data.signal: Capacity and materials (CEO Farouq Tuweiq, CFO Lynn Hutkin): 'capacity is not a major concern today', and as the Slovakia site comes online it adds flexibility; 'the more interesting challenge is supply-chain availability of materials'. Inventories rose $32 million as additional raw materials were procured for first-half orders, and inventory turns are expected to stay challenged near term as Bel builds inventory for its growth projections. Capital expenditures were $4.9 million in the first half of 2026, with slightly higher CapEx planned for the second half on throughput and quick-ROI projects.
quarterly_data.figure: inventories up $32 million; first-half CapEx $4.9 million

quarterly_data.signal: European defense (CEO Farouq Tuweiq): Bel's Slovakia facility (historically its industrial power factory) gained certification as a defense manufacturer in Europe, and Q2 brought an additional eight project wins from European defense customers for the site after one win last quarter - ahead of the plan to have wins by end of 2026. Sales are anticipated to begin in the latter part of 2027; the wins span diverse platforms with no dominant customer and are 'multimillion-dollar opportunities collectively over the life cycle of the programs'. On missile stockpile replenishment, orders are increasing but government funding has not yet caught up.
quarterly_data.figure: eight European defense project wins in Q2; sales expected from latter part of 2027
